intro.title: Build LRU cache class
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Least Recently Used (LRU) Cache class in JavaScript. An LRU cache is a data structure that stores a limited number of items, automatically removing the least recently used one when full to make space for new entries. You'll learn to implement this using core JavaScript constructs like classes, objects, and arrays to manage the cache's size and access order. This project will help you understand how caching works to optimize data retrieval in applications. By the end, you'll have a functional LRU Cache that can store, retrieve, and efficiently manage key-value pairs.
intro.usecase: An LRU cache is essential in web applications where you need to manage limited memory while keeping frequently accessed data readily available. You'll see this pattern in browser caching systems that store recently visited web pages for faster back/forward navigation, or in e-commerce product listing pages that cache recently viewed items. As a developer, you might implement an LRU cache for an analytics dashboard that caches frequently requested chart data, or for a search component that remembers recent queries to provide instant suggestions. This ensures optimal performance while preventing memory overflow in real-world applications.
